paper.title: Boosting MLLM Spatial Reasoning with Geometrically Referenced 3D Scene Representations

anchored_sections: Method (3D Scene Analysis, Language-Based Geometric Reasoning, Text-Image Association)
Experiments (Benchmarks, Implementation Details, Evaluation Results, Ablation Study, Qualitative Examples)
coverage.notes: Full-paper grounded analysis covering motivation, algorithmic formulation, occlusion pruning, prompt structure, VSI-Bench and MindCube benchmarks, ablations, sparse qualitative cases, and critical comparison with 3D-MLLM/agent literature.

claims.claim: GR3D introduces geometrically referenced 3D scene representations that couple 2D visual cues with ID-indexed 3D geometric textual descriptions in a training-free framework.
Depth-based occlusion pruning eliminates occluded object tags by comparing projected canonical depth z against dense depth map D(i, j) at minimal computational cost.
GR3D boosts zero-shot spatial reasoning across multiple MLLMs, pushing GPT-5 from 50.3% to 59.8% (+9.5%) on VSI-Bench and from 55.0% to 66.8% (+11.8%) on MindCube, establishing new SOTA.
Explicit 2D-3D visual grounding via ID stamps is necessary; providing geometric text without image annotations yields zero gain over base GPT-5 (50.3% vs 50.3%).
Spatial anchoring allows MLLMs to deduce coordinates of unannotated small objects from nearby annotated anchors, enhancing robustness against missing detections in sparse views.
